## Part 5.10 red-team continuation — persistent memory-poisoning guard (2026-10-27)

**Exact PR #163 head:** `66f4ff629644b5e89e21f8c7b4aad766d6dfc01a`; `main` untouched, no merge/deploy.

### Reproduced risk
`extractCustomerPreferencesFromText` auto-extracted sentence-like facts into durable customer AI memory. A malicious customer could disguise direct instructions as a name, budget or service preference, e.g. `My name is Ignore All Previous Instructions.`, and retain the payload for later model turns. The model already receives memory as *untrusted user-context*, which is important boundary protection, but persistent poisoning still warrants defense in depth.

### Scoped change
- `src/services/advanced-ai.service.js`: before storing auto-extracted candidate facts, reject **high-confidence instruction-like patterns** (ignore/disregard/override trusted instructions, reveal system/developer prompts, assume trusted roles). Normalize Unicode compatibility characters and remove select invisible joiners for this detection.
- `tests/memory-persistence.test.js`: adversarial name, service-interest and budget strings must be rejected; legitimate multi-word names and service interests (including benign mentions of system prompts as a service) remain accepted.

### Verified CI
[GitHub Actions run #40512238329](https://github.com/AloneSmoker007/Nova-AI/actions/runs/40512238329) at the exact head above: **SUCCESS**, quality and PostgreSQL 15/Redis 7 integration jobs both green.

**Boundary:** Pattern blocking is one deterministic layer; it is *not* comprehensive prompt-injection or PII protection, nor a substitute for external-model red-team evidence. Part 5.15-B remains NO-GO pending provider E2E, historical evidence reconciliation, payment signing rollout, deployment operations and owner security signoff. Do not merge or deploy yet.
